summary: gcp-log-poc exfiltrates full process environment to hardcoded GCP project at install and import time
details: gcp-log-poc 0.0.2 performs installer-side data exfiltration from two auto-executing entry points. setup.py (sdist build) and gcp_log_poc/__init__.py (every `import gcp_log_poc`) base64-decode an embedded Google Cloud service-account JSON containing a live RSA private key for pypi-log-writer@nginxinc.iam.gserviceaccount.com, authenticate to GCP project `nginxinc`, and POST a Cloud Logging entry containing dict(os.environ), hostname, user, cwd, Python/OS version, and the installer's public IP (fetched from api.ipify.org) to the `python-smoke-test` logger. The full environment dump captures any AWS/GCP/GitHub/CI tokens, database passwords, and API keys set in the installer's shell or CI environment and ships them to the author-controlled GCP sink. The destination credential and project are concealed behind a base64 blob (`_B64_SA`) decoded at runtime, hiding the hardcoded destination from casual inspection. Behavior is unrelated to any stated 'logging PoC' purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
